| RPR-10 | UI/API | Make mode explicit; default to business-logic parity; display refusal/deviation/certificate details. |
| RPR-11 | tests | Add unit, integration, MySQL, complete scenario, no-look-ahead, and Production/Replay comparison tests below. |
| RPR-12 | docs | Update architecture, rules, changelog, investigation, operational runbook, and parity contract. |

## 8. Error handling, concurrency, and transactions

- Replay-state creation is isolated and must be consistent for one profile version.
- Business-logic-parity evidence validation happens before replay execution; no
  partial shadow run may be labelled a parity run.
- Replay output writes are transactionally isolated by `test_run_id`; a failed
  run records its failure and certificate status without changing Production.
- Replay must not lock Production wallet/position rows for business mutation.
- Replay-profile/state reads must not expose credentials and must log only IDs,
  UTC times, symbol counts, mode, and evidence result.
- Cancellation preserves isolated run evidence and cannot leave a completed
  parity certificate.

## 9. Logging and observability registry

| ID | Event | Mandatory fields |
|---|---|---|
| RPR-L-01 | virtual starting state created/refused | runId, mode, profile ID/version, virtual balances/position counts, config fingerprint, reason |
| RPR-L-02 | evidence qualified/refused | runId, symbol(s), from/to UTC, candle/price/orderbook/derivatives status, gap counts |
| RPR-L-03 | shadow execution decision | runId, symbol, signal/candle ID, decision code, shared-policy source, replay state ID |
| RPR-L-04 | parity mismatch | runId, field, Production value, replay value, evidence reference, severity |
| RPR-L-05 | certificate completed | runId, claim, matched/mismatched field counts, simulation deviations, duration |
| RPR-L-06 | retired path blocked | runId, removed/experimental feature ID, requested source, outcome |

## 10. Database/configuration/trading impact

- **Database:** additive replay account/snapshot/certificate/evidence schema and any
  required durable historical derivatives observations. Applied migrations are
  never edited. Archive migration/retention is mandatory before deletion of
  retired Replay-only output tables.
- **Configuration:** add replay mode/evidence policy only. Production defaults
  and trading configuration remain unchanged.
- **Trading behaviour:** NONE. Production is read-only to this feature and no
  live/paper Production decision, wallet mutation, position, or protection
  rule may change.
- **Replay behaviour:** baseline becomes evidence-qualified business-logic parity
  or explicitly labelled simulation; retired experimental paths are removed or
  isolated only as approved above.

## 11. Test and validation registry

| ID | Required proof |
|---|---|
| RPR-T-01 | The same profile inputs produce equal Production/replay sizing, reserve, daily budget, daily-loss, and global-position-limit decisions through shared policies. |
| RPR-T-01a | Replay refuses `BUSINESS_LOGIC_PARITY` when no immutable replay account profile is selected; it must never silently use a Production wallet row. |
| RPR-T-02 | A missing, unresolved, rejected, or coverage-gapped price event refuses business-logic parity and labels simulation correctly. |
| RPR-T-03 | Price-event/signal same-time ordering matches Production for TP, SL, profit lock, normal exit, and signal SELL. |
| RPR-T-04 | End-to-end initial BUY, progressive add, target extension, rebase, stop, profit lock, near-TP partial harvest, terminal exit, and P&L lifecycle match field-for-field. |
| RPR-T-05 | Historical order book/derivatives use only as-of persisted data; missing evidence refuses parity; no live HTTP occurs. |
| RPR-T-05a | Replay never reads a Production wallet settings row or calls a Binance minimum-notional endpoint; profile values drive the same pure minimum-order decision. |
| RPR-T-06 | Multi-symbol global wallet/max-position test proves no isolated-symbol bypass. |
| RPR-T-07 | Cancellation/error tests prove Production tables remain unchanged and certificates cannot falsely pass. |
| RPR-T-08 | MySQL migration and transaction tests use a disposable database. |
| RPR-T-09 | Dataset and database replay inputs produce equivalent output for the same qualified evidence, or one path is removed. |
| RPR-T-10 | Removal tests prove baseline Replay cannot invoke FIX-11K, FIX-11Q, or pre-FIX-122 paths. |
| RPR-T-11 | Real historical parity suite compares selected known Production windows and produces stored certificates. |

## 12. Risks, rollback, and acceptance

- Risk: historical data required for verified parity may not exist. Mitigation:
  refuse parity and use clearly labelled simulation; do not invent evidence.
- Risk: snapshot schema increases storage. Mitigation: bounded retention and
  archive strategy, never deletion of active/investigation evidence.
- Risk: retiring observers breaks historical UI/archive reads. Mitigation:
  migration and archive/export compatibility tests before removal.
- Rollback: disable new business-logic-parity mode and retain existing archived
  output; Production requires no rollback because it is never mutated.

Acceptance requires: all registry IDs reconciled; no unregistered code change;
all test evidence green; disposable MySQL validation; complete source review by
Claude; Codex verification of the exact reviewed revision; and explicit user
authorization after both agents approve this same document.

agent-docs\FINAL_CHANGE_SPECIFICATION_RPR-0.9.1.md:36:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261015-005147\round01-codex.stderr.txt:16496:agent-docs\runs\20261011-023447\round01-codex.stderr.txt:1868:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-230204\round01-claude.prompt.txt:60:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.prompt.txt:60:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-claude.prompt.txt:60:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

agent-docs\runs\20261011-224337\round01-codex.stderr.txt:1877:**Recorded-entry fixtures (review finding F1).** A lifecycle comparison is seeded from Production's recorded entries, which live in the account tables that Replay may not read. The recorded entries therefore reach Replay only as an **immutable entry-fixture dataset**, prepared by a separate read-only extraction that runs outside the Replay execution boundary and is never part of a Replay run. Each fixture holds: symbol, position identifier, recorded entry time, execution price and the observed-at time of that price, the entry signal identifier, the normalised fixed-notional basis (the recorded quantity is kept for audit and is not used for sizing), initial stop loss and take profit, entry scores, entry-consumption state, and the protection state at entry. The dataset has a content hash recorded in the run certificate. Replay reads the fixture file or Replay-owned fixture table only; the forbidden-dependency guard still applies to every account table. The extraction queries and their results are kept as evidence (E09).

## FINDINGS

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — FIX-156 cannot safely be finished from the current code.** The active Replay path still invokes shared Production BUY authority, its repositories, and validation. This violates the documented Replay-local BUY/lifecycle requirement and can reintroduce wallet/configuration dependencies transitively.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — The SQL allow-list is not an effective boundary.** `ReplayAccessPolicy` is called only by two new stores; the worker and shadow service execute many direct SQL statements without it. The policy cannot intercept or reject those paths.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — A prohibited shared-table write remains reachable.** When `shared-market.mode=LIVE`, the Replay worker opens `CandleInputAudit`, whose capture method inserts into `shared_candle_input_audit`. This is outside the sole stated `fix122_evaluation` exception.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — The new parity certificate, trace, output, and coverage tables are unused.** Source search found only their migration definitions and allow-list test references—not a writer, comparator, or lifecycle integration. The old `EXACT_PRICE_REPLAY` label still means merely “at least one event exists,” not complete price-path coverage.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — Profile seeding is not wired.** Replay now calls `ReplayPolicyProfileStore.require(runId)` before execution, but no in-code caller creates/inserts a profile. A normal run will refuse unless data is externally pre-seeded; no qualified fixture-creation flow is evidenced.

- **PROJECT EVIDENCE — The review package is internally inconsistent.** The Jean record says USR-REV-001/002 were accepted and explicitly closed, while the implementation status report still says both are open. The canonical change specification is also an unapproved RPR-0.4 draft, not RPR-0.9.12.

- **AGENT INFERENCE — Boundary claims are presently unsound.** A hand-coded allow-list that no existing SQL lifecycle uses cannot establish table/operation isolation, and no T156-09/T156-09a/T156-09b-quality proof exists.

- **AGENT INFERENCE — Parity results would be vulnerable to false positives.** Incomplete price coverage, current configuration dependencies, and production-service reachability permit look-ahead/configuration drift and Replay/Production divergence while retaining optimistic labels.

- **AGENT INFERENCE — Do not treat Jean’s closure as technical completion.** It authorizes continued Replay-only work, but the current code does not satisfy the closure criteria described in the same record.
